item.title: [Recap] Julian Champagnie (SAS): Julian Champagnie tallied 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Julian Champagnie tallied 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

Champagnie made four of the Spurs’ 17 three-pointers on Saturday, the second time this season he’s made at least that many in a game. While the rebounds were solid, Champagnie is most valuable to managers needing points and three-pointers. Tobias Harris’ continued absence makes Champagnie a little more important for offensive spacing reasons, but he’s only worth a look in deep leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Stephon Castle (SAS): Stephon Castle amassed 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Stephon Castle amassed 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

Castle has scored in double figures in nine of 10 games this season, except for his scoreless effort in an October 31 win over the Timberwolves. Like the other starters, Castle did not play in the fourth quarter of Saturday’s victory, which likely robbed him of chances to post better numbers. His current value hasn’t aligned with his top-60 ADP, but Castle is closing in on the top-100 in eight- and nine-cat formats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Devin Vassell (SAS): Devin Vassell notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Devin Vassell notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

One of three Spurs starters to make multiple three-pointers, Vassell is averaging 1.6 per game this season. Despite his low field-goal percentage, the Spurs wing provides solid middle-round value in 12-team formats. With the Spurs playing four games next week, Vassell may be worth a look for those needing three-pointers and steals, as he’s available in 48 percent of Yahoo leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Victor Wembanyama (SAS): Victor Wembanyama finished Saturday’s rout of the Trail Blazers with 29 points (9-of-13 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers.
item.description:
Victor Wembanyama finished Saturday’s rout of the Trail Blazers with 29 points (9-of-13 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers.

While the final stat line wasn’t as robust as his showing in Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks, Wembanyama thoroughly outplayed Portland’s Donovan Clingan on Saturday. The Spurs center only played 24 minutes, as San Antonio outscored Portland 87-56 in the second and third quarters. Wemby and the other Spurs starters watched the entire fourth quarter from the bench, which may have annoyed some fantasy managers hoping for an elite stat line. The Spurs play four games next week, starting with the Suns on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Scoot Henderson (POR): Scoot Henderson produced 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Scoot Henderson produced 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.

Unfortunately for fantasy managers who believed a move into the starting lineup would improve Henderson’s value, he hasn’t delivered. Since Ja Morant (hamstring) went down in an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, Scoot’s category-league value has ranked outside the top-300 in nine-cat formats. Unsurprisingly, Jrue Holiday (11 points, one steal and one three-pointer) has been far more valuable, regardless of league format. Portland plays three games next week, starting with a home back-to-back against the Thunder on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven assists and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Damian Lillard finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven assists and two three-pointers.

Lillard’s streak of games with at least 20 points ended at four on Saturday, with the veteran point guard also attempting a season-low eight shots from the field. Lillard shot a solid percentage from the field, but many expected more, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined. The good news is that Lillard played both games of Portland’s back-to-back. Saturday’s game was a blowout, so he played only 20 minutes.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija tallied 15 points (5-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Deni Avdija tallied 15 points (5-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.

Avdija led the Trail Blazers in points and field-goal attempts on Saturday, but the overall stat line was underwhelming. Deni didn’t shoot well from the field and recorded just one assist. Surprisingly, Avdija’s fantasy value has slipped after Ja Morant’s hamstring injury. Over the last five games, he sits just outside the top-200 in nine-cat formats. Avdija will look to contribute more when Portland hosts Oklahoma City on Tuesday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Yang Hansen (POR): Yang Hansen finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (3-of-7 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Yang Hansen finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (3-of-7 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer.

There’s no such thing as “garbage time"; those minutes are vital for non-rotation players looking to give their coaches a reason to call their name when the stakes are higher. While Yang’s showing against the Spurs is unlikely to make him a fixture in the Trail Blazers’ rotation, it was a step forward. The former first-round pick recorded his first double-double, establishing new career highs in points and rebounds. As good as it was to see him perform well, Yang should still be rostered only in dynasty leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Anthony Black (ORL): Anthony Black finished Saturday’s overtime loss to the Warriors with 18 points (7-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, four steals, three blocks and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Anthony Black finished Saturday’s overtime loss to the Warriors with 18 points (7-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, four steals, three blocks and two three-pointers.

Black didn’t have a great night shooting the basketball, but his final stat line included seven defensive contributions and six assists. Unfortunately, the Magic guard was not on the floor for the second half of overtime, as cramping sidelined Black with 2:47 remaining in the period. Orlando doesn’t play again until Tuesday against the Kings; hopefully, that’s enough time for Black to rehydrate and play without any issues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Stephen Curry (GSW): Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday.
item.description:
Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday.

Curry’s sublime start to the year continued in this one as he topped the 40-point plateau for the second time in eight games. His signature sequence came in the final minute of regulation when he knocked down a three-pointer before sinking a pair of free throws and converting a go-ahead layup in the closing seconds. He added five points in overtime as Golden State was finally able to pull away for good. The 38-year-old legend has delivered first-round fantasy value so far, averaging 31.3 points through eight games. Are you not entertained? The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Franz Wagner (ORL): Franz Wagner delivered a team-high 30 points (11-of-22 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, 11 assists and two steals over 30 minutes in an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.
item.description:
Franz Wagner delivered a team-high 30 points (11-of-22 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, 11 assists and two steals over 30 minutes in an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.

Wagner continues to serve as Orlando’s main option with Paolo Banchero (ankle) likely out until at least late November. He knocked down just 3-of-7 from three-point range, but dished out double-digit assists for the fourth time in his last five contests. He’s averaging 20.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, 8.8 assists and 1.3 steals through nine games. The Magic have a three-game week on tap that features matchups against the Kings, Jazz and Bucks.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in an overtime victory over the Magic on Saturday.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks across 37 minutes in an overtime victory over the Magic on Saturday.

Lendeborg continues to be a revelation for Golden State, surpassing the 20-point plateau for the fifth time in 10 games to open his rookie campaign. He and franchise icon Stephen Curry combined for 64 points in a thrilling overtime victory, accounting for more than half of the Warriors’ offensive output. He came through in the clutch, scoring seven of his 23 points in overtime. The 24-year-old rookie sensation should be rostered in all fantasy formats, as he’s quickly establishing himself as a high-volume scoring threat in Golden State’s offense. The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Wendell Carter (ORL): Wendell Carter Jr. contributed 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds and two blocks over 40 minutes during an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.
item.description:
Wendell Carter Jr. contributed 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds and two blocks over 40 minutes during an overtime loss to the Warriors on Saturday.

Carter had little trouble handling an undersized Golden State squad to notch his second straight double-double. He was a perfect 3-for-3 from three-point range, but missed five times from the free-throw line in this one, which wound up mattering in a close contest. The 27-year-old former first-round pick has delivered fifth-round fantasy value this season, averaging 14.8 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks through nine games. The Magic have a three-game week on tap that features matchups against the Kings, Jazz and Bucks.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Amen Thompson (HOU): Amen Thompson tallied 17 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, one steal and four blocks in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
item.description:
Amen Thompson tallied 17 points (7-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, one steal and four blocks in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.

Thompson didn’t record an assist on Saturday, the first time that’s happened this season. The good news for fantasy managers is that he blocked four shots, double his total entering Saturday. While Thompson is providing top-100 value, his averages have decreased across the board compared to 2025-26. The Rockets open a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Nuggets.

item.description:
Jabari Smith Jr. notched 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.

Smith finished one rebound shy of a double-double and recorded a complete stat line in Saturday’s defeat. Over three weeks, the Rockets forward has provided top-25 value in 12-team formats. Given Smith’s fantasy production for most of his career, fantasy managers should look into what they can get for him. For the right return, selling high on Smith wouldn’t be a bad idea.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Fred VanVleet (HOU): Fred VanVleet amassed 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.
item.description:
Fred VanVleet amassed 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Suns.

VanVleet’s four three-pointers matched his season high, a number he’s hit on three occasions in eight games. The overall field-goal percentage pushed the Rockets’ point guard over 40 percent for the season, and that’s around where VanVleet has hovered for most of his career. Even with the low field-goal percentage, VanVleet does enough in other categories to provide reliable middle-round value when healthy.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kevin Durant (HOU): Kevin Durant finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Kevin Durant finished Saturday’s loss to the Suns with 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer.

Durant had only one official field-goal attempt in the first half, scoring six points thanks to his going 4-of-5 from the foul line. He took 13 shots in the second half and made four, which hurt KD’s shooting efficiency. He did grab 10 rebounds, finishing with his first double-double of the season. The Rockets play four games next week, starting with the Nuggets on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accumulated a game-high 30 points (11-of-20 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists and one block over 29 minutes to propel the Thunder to a 114-75 blowout win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accumulated a game-high 30 points (11-of-20 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists and one block over 29 minutes to propel the Thunder to a 114-75 blowout win over the Wizards.

Gilgeous-Alexander scored 30 points in just three quarters to help Oklahoma City cruise to a relatively easy 39-point victory on the second night of a back-to-back. The 28-year-old scoring machine is averaging a sublime 29.9 points through 10 games, topping 30 points in exactly half of those contests. The Thunder are back in action with a busy four-game week that includes back-to-back showdowns against the Trail Blazers in addition to road tilts against the Clippers and Kings.

George Bissell

item.title: [Injury] Ja Morant (POR): Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori said on Saturday that Ja Morant (hamstring) “may not be out for as long as we thought.”
item.description:
Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori said on Saturday that Ja Morant (hamstring) “may not be out for as long as we thought.”

Morant, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain during an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, was to be re-evaluated towards the end of November. However, according to Nori, a doctor in Los Angeles evaluated Morant and gave him a positive outlook on the injury. That’s good news for those rostering the athletic point guard, who was fitting in well with his new teammates at the time of the injury. Scoot Henderson will start until Morant is healthy enough to play.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Larry Nance (IND): Larry Nance Jr. shot 5-of-7 from the field in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets, scoring 15 points with two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers.
item.description:

Nance was in a groove on Saturday, matching his career high with five three-pointers. The veteran forward/center needed just seven attempts to reach that mark, a welcome development after Nance began the season shooting 5-for-17 from deep. He still can’t be relied on in most fantasy leagues, but Nance played 13 minutes while fellow reserve Jay Huff (zero points, three rebounds) played 10 minutes.

item.title: [Recap] Toumani Camara (POR): Toumani Camara notched 18 points (7-of-12 FGs), six rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Toumani Camara notched 18 points (7-of-12 FGs), six rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.

Despite being low on the Trail Blazers’ offensive pecking order, Camara has provided consistent value this season. He’s scored at least nine points in all eight games, cracking double figures in seven. Against the Lakers, Camara hit four three-pointers, the fifth time this season he’s made at least that many in a game. Surprisingly, there was no defensive production to speak of, but those rostering Camara should be pleased with the reliable offensive output.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Donovan Clingan (POR): Donovan Clingan finished Friday’s loss to the Lakers with 17 points (6-of-8 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers.
item.description:
Donovan Clingan finished Friday’s loss to the Lakers with 17 points (6-of-8 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers.

Clingan seems to be hitting his stride after an inconsistent start to the season. The 7-foot-2 center has recorded a double-double in three straight games, and he shot 3-of-5 from beyond the arc against the Lakers. Over the last week, Clingan has provided second-round value in nine-cat formats. However, his final game of the week will offer a significant challenge, as the Trail Blazers host the Spurs on Saturday.

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija recorded 22 points (6-of-12 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Deni Avdija recorded 22 points (6-of-12 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.

Avdija shot well from the field and finished one rebound shy of a triple-double. However, he also recorded a season-high eight turnovers. In the Trail Blazers’ last four games, Avdija has dished out 30 assists, taking on even more playmaking responsibilities with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined. Also, Friday’s eight turnovers were a departure from the norm, as Deni had not committed more than three in any game this season.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard accounted for 22 points (5-of-13 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Damian Lillard accounted for 22 points (5-of-13 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.

Lillard led the team in points on Friday, but the production was lacking outside of points and three-pointers. He has scored at least 20 points in each of those contests, which is the main reason Lillard has provided fifth-round value over the last week.

item.title: [Recap] Austin Reaves (LAL): Austin Reaves tallied 25 points (8-of-22 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Austin Reaves tallied 25 points (8-of-22 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

Reaves struggled to begin Friday’s game, missing his first seven shots. However, he shone in the second and fourth quarters, shooting 7-of-12 from the field and scoring 23 of his 25 points. Even with Friday’s poor shooting, Reaves is shooting nearly 51 percent from the field. His fantasy value hasn’t aligned with his top-25 ADP, but Reaves has been a top-50 player through the Lakers’ first 10 games.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:

Through 10 games, Kessler has been an excellent center for managers punting free-throw percentage.

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
item.description:
Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.

Dončić finished Friday’s victory with his 11th 50-point game, moving past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Allen Iverson to land in tenth on the league’s all-time list. But that wasn’t the only history the Lakers star made on Friday. Dončić has tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds, and five assists in seven straight games, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in league history. Also, Dončić, who outscored Portland 20-15 in the third quarter, has scored at least 40 points in four straight games. He’s on an incredible run, which is great for those rostering Dončić.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum accumulated a game-high 34 points (9-of-16 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, nine assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes, leading the Celtics to a 119-80 blowout win over the Hornets on Friday.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum accumulated a game-high 34 points (9-of-16 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, nine assists, one steal and one block in 29 minutes, leading the Celtics to a 119-80 blowout win over the Hornets on Friday.

Simply put, Tatum loves playing in North Carolina. The 28-year-old franchise cornerstone reached the 30-point plateau with a nifty reverse layup midway through the third quarter as Boston continued pulling away, eventually opening up a near 40-point lead by the end of the third quarter. He put the finishing touch on his monster evening by knocking down his 11th free throw of the night in the final minute of the quarter, finishing just shy of a triple-double in a monster statsheet-stuffing effort. The lopsided score allowed him to sit out the fourth, otherwise he may have been in line for an even bigger performance. He’s delivered top-30 fantasy value in the early stages of the season, recording four 30-point efforts in his first eight games. The Celtics close out the week with a road tilt against the Bucks on Sunday before kicking off a three-game week with road matchups against the 76ers and Raptors.

George Bissell

He’s shown some signs of life recently after a rough start to his Hornets debut.

item.title: [Recap] Stephen Curry (GSW): Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday.
item.description:
Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 29 points (9-of-19 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 120-100 win over the Heat on Thursday.

Despite a rough start to this game, Curry got going in the third quarter. After scoring seven points on 2-of-10 shooting in the first half, he scored 14 points in the third quarter alone and eight more points in the fourth to steal the win for Golden State. Curry has been unbelievable to start the season, which has him ranked as one of the best players in fantasy basketball to this point. He’ll look to stay hot against the Magic to wrap up the week on Saturday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg posted a full line on Thursday with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Heat.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg posted a full line on Thursday with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Heat.

Lendeborg has been one of the best rookies in the league this season, which has worked out well for fantasy managers, especially as of late. Since he was held to six points against the Lakers last week, he has averaged 23.3 points,5.7 rebounds, 5.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 3.0 triples per game. Lendeborg has been able to make an impact on both ends of the floor, with his only weakness in fantasy basketball being too many turnovers.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Will Richard (GSW): Will Richard started on Thursday and finished with 10 points (4-of-6 FGs), one rebound, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Heat.
item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), two rebounds, eight assists, one steal, four three-pointers and five turnovers in a 120-100 loss to the Warriors on Thursday.
item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Devin Booker (PHX): Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.

item.title: [Recap] Miles Bridges (PHX): Miles Bridges stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 13 rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Magic.

Over his last four games, Bridges has averaged 20.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.3 steals, 1.0 block and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 51.8 percent from the free throw line. Given his production in those two starts and Isaiah Jackson’s inability to avoid silly fouls, Lopez may have the starting center job for the foreseeable future. Jackson, who has committed at least four fouls in six of his eight games, played 13 minutes against the Heat and finished with two points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.

Hachimura has gotten off to a relatively slow start with the Clippers, shooting 37.3 percent from the field and 68.4 percent from the foul line. Add inconsistent production in assists, steals and blocks, and rostering Hachimura in some 10-team leagues isn’t worth discussing. He had a productive night against the Heat, with the seven assists being more than double his total entering the night (three). For Hachimura to be someone you can roster in shallow leagues after the Clippers get guys like Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal back, nights like Wednesday have to become the norm.

item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.

Mitchell’s start to the season has been better than most fantasy managers expected, with the Heat guard providing top-50 per-game value. He couldn’t buy a three-pointer on Wednesday, missing all five attempts, but Mitchell offered excellent production in assists and steals. And even with Wednesday’s poor shooting, Mitchell is still shooting 50 percent from the field this season.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Bam Adebayo (MIA): Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.

This was a big night for Adebayo, who recorded his first double-double of the season with new highs in points and rebounds. Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Klay Thompson (MIA): Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
item.description:
Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.

Thompson had his best game of the season on Wednesday, shooting 8-of-17 from beyond the arc. His last three-pointer was the most important, as the Heat guard/forward hit one from the left corner with one second remaining in overtime to give Miami the win. Inconsistent in his first five games, Thompson has scored at least 19 points in three straight. Could he be returning to fantasy relevance? The Heat play two more games this week, so it may not be a bad time to stream Klay if you need three-pointers.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Naji Marshall (DAL): Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.

The Mavericks had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and looked set to get blown out. However, Marshall got going in the second half, shooting 7-of-9 from the field and scoring 17 points. Marshall remains a player who can be rostered in deep leagues, even though he’ll come off the bench on most nights.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.

After shooting 3-of-19 from the field in Monday’s loss to the Kings, Flagg got off to a terribly slow start on Wednesday. The reigning Rookie of the Year missed all seven of his shots in the first quarter and started 1-of-11 from the field. The good news is that Flagg shot 6-of-8 the rest of the way. Add in the rebounds and assists, and the final stat line was solid, but category managers would have wanted to see more defensive stats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving amassed 29 points (9-of-27 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving amassed 29 points (9-of-27 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.

Active after sitting out Monday’s loss to the Kings, Irving played 36 minutes in the 112-111 thriller. He had a chance to put the Mavericks ahead in the final seconds of regulation, but the shot missed. Irving has provided excellent fantasy value so far, but availability remains a concern.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Zuby Ejiofor (ATL): Zuby Ejiofor got 11 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, and a three in 17 minutes against the Wizards.
item.description:
Zuby Ejiofor got 11 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, and a three in 17 minutes against the Wizards.

The big man from St. John’s had an impact off the bench in this game and was a big factor in why the Hawks got big leads when the bench was in the game. Asa Newell (toe) left the game early and Jock Landale (hip) is already out, so if you wanted to stream in Zuby in deeper redraft leagues, he could have some value for rebounds. In dynasty leagues, you should be happy that he had this performance and flashed what he might be capable of with more minutes.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Onyeka Okongwu (ATL): Onyeka Okongwu had a good 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in 120-105 win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Onyeka Okongwu had a good 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in 120-105 win over the Wizards.

Okongwu has been mildly disappointing this season, so it was good to see him have a good game. He got some more stocks which have been lacking at this point. The minutes aren’t going anywhere, so he should continue to have this role barring injury. In dynasty, if he were to ever get traded, his role could be in jeopardy given the fact that he’s an undersized center who doesn’t defend at a super high level.

item.title: [Recap] Dyson Daniels (ATL): Dyson Daniels put up 8 points (4-of-13 FGs), a career high 17 rebounds, and eight assists on Wednesday against the Wizards.
item.description:
Dyson Daniels put up 8 points (4-of-13 FGs), a career high 17 rebounds, and eight assists on Wednesday against the Wizards.

Dyson didn’t score the ball, but he did have a career high 17 rebounds in this game. Dyson’s offense hasn’t gotten back to where it was in his third year, and the lack of a three-point shot will hinder him, but the defense has been awesome, and he’s been what you would’ve hoped for when you drafted him with most of his value coming from steals and good rebounds from a guard.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Kingston Flemings (ATL): Kingston Flemings had 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Wizards.
item.description:
Kingston Flemings had 14 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Wizards.

In his first start of his career, he played well and you felt his imprint on the game. It was said on the broadcast that it was CJ McCollum’s idea for Kingston to start and get into a rhythm. It is notable that Kingston played 23 minutes when CJ played 25 minutes. His ability to collapse a defense with his speed was on full display. We’ll see if this is a permanent change, but he clearly looked good in this game.

Brian Taylor
